answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 for a 90-day horizon before it can bid on jobs; the same deposit cannot back two identities at once. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000, with borrowing costs and lost access to that capital. Identities may multiply like grains in a dune, but each must bring fresh collateral: an echo of an existing agent gains no free bidding power.
